title: CodeEvolve: an open source evolutionary coding agent for algorithmic discovery and optimization

mechanism.domainTask: Open-source evolutionary framework for algorithmic discovery and executable program optimization
mechanism.populationDetail: Island solution and prompt populations evolve independently with migration; solution ancestry is explicitly represented as rooted trees, while each island also has a separate MAP-Elites archive.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Each island maintains a MAP-Elites/CVT-MAP-Elites archive with the highest-fitness solution per user-defined feature cell.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Successful solutions are added to island pools; per-cell archive elites use fitter-than-incumbent replacement, and top solutions migrate between islands. Global population pruning is not specified.
mechanism.generationDetail: One target solution is edited through SEARCH/REPLACE with its prompt and, for exploitation, ancestors; multiple inspiration solutions provide contextual patterns that the paper calls semantic crossover, while exploration first meta-prompts the instructions.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: h returns a vector of task metrics, but fsol is a scalar fitness used for selection; failed executions receive zero fitness and logs are stored for later prompt context.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: One target solution is directly edited; ancestor lineage context and multiple inspirations are separate inputs. The exact population/archive sampling mix depends on configuration.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Joint evolution of prompt and solution populations with ancestry, per-island QD archives, inspiration-based semantic crossover, and adaptive operator scheduling.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/CODEEVOLVE an open-source evolutionary framework for algorithmic discovery and optimization.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Hybrid population contains island organization and explicit tree lineages alongside a separate QD archive. The paper calls multiple inspiration inputs semantic crossover, but only one target solution is directly edited; record the boundary instead of treating inspiration count as true parent count. Model ensemble count and archive/pool sampling mix are configuration-dependent.
